A short essay on why small things stay understandable: every part has to earn its place, and whatever does not is cut. We think the habit matters more than the size.

The author shows it with a plain example. A function that fits on one screen gets read, questioned and improved. One that does not gets trusted and left alone, and that is how mistakes stay for years.

What we take from it for our own work is modest. Keep the piece small enough that someone else can hold all of it in their head at once.
